name: llm-d vLLM Model-Aware Readiness Probes guide
notes: Three lifecycle stages are distinguished: Container Running (Kubernetes), API Server Ready (the OpenAI-compatible server accepting connections), and Model Loaded. The core statement: 'The vLLM /health endpoint only indicates that the server process is running, not that models are loaded and ready to serve.' /health returns 200 immediately at server start and does not wait for model loading; /v1/models returns 503 or connection-refused during loading and 200 with model metadata once ready, so it is the model-aware probe. Recommended probe shape uses /health only for liveness and /v1/models for both startupProbe and readinessProbe, with a startupProbe failureThreshold of 60 at a 30s period, which the doc computes as a 30 minute maximum startup time. Ports differ by role: prefill 8000, decode 8200 (proxied through a sidecar), standalone 8000, and 'Always configure probes to match the pod serving port.' Consequences listed for using only basic health checks: premature traffic routing to pods that are not ready, failed requests during model loading, 'Need for arbitrary sleep times in deployment pipelines', and unreliable E2E testing. Common causes of a stuck NotReady pod: 'Model download taking longer than the failureThreshold allows', insufficient CPU/memory/GPU, wrong probe port, network issues preventing model download; solutions include pre-downloading models with init containers or persistent volumes. Cites vLLM #6073 as the reason no dedicated /ready endpoint exists.
